Some industry commentary regarding a few claims recently on memory + Softbank Turbine defaulting.

- On claims that LTAs are "meaningless while prices fall": 

$MU: "strategic customer agreements cannot be unilaterally canceled.  Customers are obligated to pay for their committed volumes whether they take delivery or not"

"These are take or pay agreements and there are no contractual outs for our customers from these agreements"

Regarding historical contracts breaking: "These LTAs that we used to have never had any binding terms." The new SCAs contain extensive contractual obligations

Regarding Elon's claims on Softbank defaulting on Turbines:

Question from Morgan Stanley to $GE Vernova CEO on whether they see cancellations or financing difficulties with counterparties on their turbine orders:

“No… we are not”

TLDR:
- Micron states LTAs/SCAs are noncancellable take/pay (where counterparties are hyperscalers). And that these types are different from historical memory cancellations. 

- On Softbank turbine orders, GE Vernova CEO Scott Strazik said it wasn't seeing customer financing disruptions, requests to exit turbine reservations, or slowdowns. 

Maybe Elon's claims are more narrow, but should be evaluated more closely given competitive interests vs. Softbank/OpenAI.

🚨 FIFA/FC will never be the same again 

This game was never perfect. What made it fun in the past was the fact people played the game in the way they saw football.

Right now, everyone is looking for the most meta things to spam them over and over again, and regardless of how many patches we get, something will be more effective and it will be spammed. This is a problem in general in the gaming community.

What EA can do? They can bring diversity at a level where people that want to have fun can survive. Right now, the difference between the main meta and fun is quite big.

1. We should have attacking AI for people that want to play possession style of football. Right now, the AI do just get in behind runs, which favour the counter attack style of football.

2. We need players ID. E-football did a great job at this.

3. We need Evolutions & SBCs that are aligned with cheap meta. These evolutions must NOT BE better than the expensive players on the market, and the most meta golds must be banned from entering evolutions so we don't end up switching from Carreras gold to Carreras evo. Diversity is important.

Ambassador @ZaluzhnyiUA in his latest essay in @pravda_eng makes a few strong points. 
Europe may be spending billions to lose the next war more efficiently. That is the uncomfortable point in Zaluzhnyi’s essay. The problem is not a shortage of drones, AI or autonomy. It is that new technology is still being pushed into military structures and doctrines built for another era.

That matters to investors too. Defence capital is chasing platforms, but the real question is whether a technology fits the way wars will actually be fought. A brilliant system with no doctrine, no integration path and no scalable procurement model is not a breakthrough. It is a science project with a valuation.

Russia’s advantage is not that every weapon is better. It is that production, electronic warfare, long-range strike, manpower and battlefield adaptation are increasingly being connected into one system of pressure.

For investors, doctrine should become part of diligence. Otherwise Europe risks buying the weapons of 2030, fighting with the institutions of 1990, and discovering that some of today’s category leaders were simply very expensive red trousers. https://t.co/Tvlcoe8Y8b

the ai trade won’t bottom until market participants finally learn *not* to value companies based on fwd pe. 

a fwd pe of 40 is not necessarily expensive if earnings grow durably over decades. a fwd pe of 4 is not cheap if earnings last 18mo then go down 90%.

a company’s value is the net present value of *all* future cash flow, not the net present value of *next year’s* cash flow.
